draft.note_text:
Subjective:
57M with hx DM, HTN, asthma c/o SOB x ~2 weeks. Wakes up SOB; SOB recurs on return home; SOB with exertion. Hemoptysis x ~3 weeks, pt reports 3-4 cups/day, only with cough. No hematemesis, no other bleeding, no gum bleeding or bruising. No fevers. No leg or calf swelling; chronic knee pain for a long time without swelling. Recent travel not reported. No ED visit; could not get an office appointment. DM: on metformin 500 mg BID, Dexcom shows post-meal spikes >200 and fasting ~150 x ~1 month. Last A1c ~7.7 (pt had diet/exercise counselling). HTN: on Norvasc, but skipping some days as home BP runs low, sometimes low 90s.

Objective:
SpO2 94% in clinic. BP 120/70 in clinic. No JVD, no carotid bruits. Lungs: rales and rhonchi, R>L, no wheeze, diminished breath sounds on R. Heart: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, known and unchanged, otherwise RRR. Abdomen soft. Extremities: 1+ nonpitting edema bilateral ankles, no calf tenderness, Homan sign negative.

Assessment:
1. SOB with hemoptysis: possible lung infection/pneumonia; concerned about PE/blood clot or other more serious cause.
2. DM, running high.
3. HTN, with low home BPs on Norvasc.

Plan:
1. Refer to ED today (doctor to call ahead) for CXR, CT chest and blood work. Treatment depends on findings. Pt states he can bike there, no questions.
2. Order repeat A1c today. Plan to increase metformin from 500 mg BID to 750 mg BID. Discuss further once acute illness resolved. F/u in ~3 weeks for DM plan.
3. Hold Norvasc for now. Reassess BP once workup done and pt returns.

additions: Hemoptysis of about 3 weeks' duration, approximately 3-4 cups of blood per day, occurring only with coughing; no hematemesis or bleeding elsewhere.
Shortness of breath for about 2 weeks, waking him from sleep and recurring on exertion, with persistent dyspnea after returning home.
Concern for pulmonary embolism or other serious cause of hemoptysis; the patient is being sent to the ED for chest x-ray, CT chest and labs. The patient plans to bike to the ED.
Home glucose monitored with Dexcom: postprandial readings well over 200 and fasting readings around 150 for about a month. Last A1c was about 7.7.
The patient had been taking Norvasc only on some days because home blood pressure ran low, sometimes in the lower 90s.
flags: Is biking to the ED safe?
Increase metformin before contrast CT and acute illness?
Is a cardiac cause being overlooked?
Hold Norvasc: was other medication use reviewed?
